statements.text: If A ⊂ S then A` is the complementary event to event A, where A ∪ A` = S and A ∩ A` = φ. Formula: $A\cup A'=S, \ A\cap A'=\phi$
The event and the complementary event are two mutually exclusive events.

context.text: In the venn diagram opposite: If S is the universal set, A ⊂ S then the complementary set of A is A`.

Imagine a class of $30$ students in which $12$ come to school by bus. The teacher picks one student at random. Let $A$ be the event "the student comes by bus". What is the probability that the student does not come by bus, that is, the probability of the complementary event $A'$?

statements.text: The set A - B (reading Al Akhbar only, not the other newspaper) is read as 'A difference B'.
If A, B are events of S, then A-B is the event of the occurrence of A and the non-occurrence of B, i.e. the occurrence of the event A only.
Note that (A - B) ∪ (A ∩ B) = A (the symbol between the two brackets is not clearly printed). Formula: $(A - B) \cup (A \cap B) = A$

context.text: Notice that: The event of reading Al Akhbar newspaper is represented by venn opposite diagram by set A while the event of reading Al Akhbar only but not other newspaper is represented by the set A - B

Suppose a sports club has $30$ students. $14$ of them play football, $10$ play volleyball, and $4$ play both games. One student is chosen at random. Let $A$ be the event "plays football" and $B$ the event "plays volleyball". What is the probability that the student plays football only, that is, the probability of $A - B$?
